statement: Kernel-checked formalization of qualitative van der Corput; advisory statement coverage pending. For every complex sequence z and fixed real C>0 with norm(z(n))<=C for all natural n, if for every fixed positive natural d the complex averages (1/N)*sum_(n<N) z(n+d)*conj(z(n)) tend to zero as N tends to infinity, then (1/N)*sum_(n<N) z(n) tends to zero. For a unit-bounded sequence, the full shifted sum differs from its N-d-term overlap correlation by norm at most d for every N,d, including N<d. The normalized finite inequality has right side 2/H+(4/H)*sum_(1<=d<H) norm(correlation(z,N,d))/N for 1<=H<=N. The phase specialization proves cancellation for exp(2*pi*i*f(n)) from cancellation for every positive fixed difference f(n+d)-f(n). All difference-cancellation hypotheses remain explicit. This does not prove the power-phase estimates or BoxRecurrence needed for Paper E Theorem 4.1, and gives no quantitative or growing-depth uniformity.
